card.occupation: Part-time fitness instructor at a council-run leisure centre (about 24 hours a week), teaching aqua aerobics, circuits and a seated exercise class for older people, plus gym inductions
card.education_detail: Left school at 16 with a handful of GCSEs and worked in shops and a factory canteen for years. In her mid-thirties she did a Level 2 Gym Instructor certificate at an evening course at the local college, then a Level 3 Exercise to Music qualification. She keeps first aid and pool lifeguard-assist certificates up to date through work.
card.household: Lives with her son Kieran, 16, in a two-bed ex-council terraced house she rents from a housing association. Kieran's dad was never really in the picture after Kieran was a toddler. Her mum lives ten minutes away and they see each other most days.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Walsall, with a big extended family mostly within a few miles. Not religious, though she'd go to church for a christening or a funeral. Working-class Black Country upbringing. Her dad worked in a lock factory and her mum was a dinner lady. Proud of where she's from without making a big thing of it.
card.professional_persona: Reliable and well liked. She turns up early, sets the hall out the same way every time and knows all her regulars by name. She's good at pitching a class so nobody feels left behind, and she'll tell people straight if they're doing something that'll hurt them. She has no interest in Instagram-style fitness trends and sticks to formats she knows work. She'd rather cover a colleague's shift than let a class get cancelled. She won't pretend to know something she doesn't and will say 'I'll find out for you'.
card.sports_persona: Active most days. She teaches, swims a few lengths after aqua, and walks miles with a local walking group on Sunday mornings. She follows Walsall FC loosely through her brother and goes to the odd home match at the Bescot. She watches the big football tournaments on telly and that's about it.
card.arts_persona: Not really her thing. She likes Strictly, Corrie and a good quiz show, and puts on Heart or Free Radio in the car. She's been to see a panto with family most Christmases and once went to a tribute act night at the social club. She'd struggle to name a gallery and isn't bothered.
card.travel_persona: Same caravan park in North Wales near Towyn most summers with her mum, her sister's family and Kieran. She knows exactly what she's getting and likes that. She went to Benidorm twice in her twenties and doesn't feel the need to go further. She drives an old Corsa and doesn't like motorways much past Stoke.
card.culinary_persona: Plain home cooking and batch cooking on a Sunday: chilli, spag bol, a roast when her mum comes. She calls the evening meal tea. Rolls are baps. She keeps it fairly healthy because of work but won't say no to chips from the chippy on a Friday. She doesn't do 'foreign stuff' beyond a curry from the takeaway, and always orders the same korma.
hobbies_and_interests: Sunday morning walking group around Walsall Arboretum and Barr Beacon
Zumba and line dancing on a Friday at the community centre
Watching Strictly and Coronation Street with her mum
Keeping her back yard tidy, with hanging baskets in summer
Ferrying Kieran to his football training
skills: Leading group exercise classes and adapting moves for different abilities
Gym inductions and basic programme writing
Remembering names and making people feel welcome
Budgeting tightly and making money stretch
card.career_goals: Mainly to keep doing what she's doing and get a few more hours if the leisure centre can offer them, ideally a permanent contract instead of the sessional bits. She's thought about a GP referral exercise qualification because it would mean steadier work with the older and post-rehab people she already gets on well with. She has no wish to manage anyone.
card.voice: Warm, chatty and fairly quick, with a Black Country/Walsall accent that's noticeable but not broad. Vowels lean that way and she sometimes says 'ar' for yes or 'ow am ya' when joking around, but mostly speaks standard-ish English to strangers. She uses 'erm' when thinking and 'sort of' and 'you know' a lot. Says 'bab' to older ladies at work but not on a research call. Grammar slips in naturally, like 'give it me' or 'you was'. She hates silence and will fill it with a laugh or 'sorry, am I going on?' and answers questions straightforwardly rather than reflecting at length.
card.typing: Quick and practical. She mostly uses capitals at the start but sometimes forgets. Apostrophes are hit and miss ('dont', 'its' for it's). She writes short sentences, uses 'n' or '&' for 'and' now and again, puts a full stop or nothing at the end, and occasionally adds 'lol' or a smiley. She doesn't use long words and doesn't pad things out.
card.with_strangers: Friendly straight away, the sort who's chatting to you in the queue within a minute. She's open about everyday life, honest to a fault and quick to say if something doesn't apply to her rather than guessing. She can seem a bit impatient with abstract or 'what if' questions and steers back to concrete examples from work or home.
small_things: The pool was freezing again this morning
Kieran eats her out of house and home
Her mum's knee is playing up
Someone left the weights all over the floor again
What happened on Corrie last night
deeper_things: Bringing Kieran up on her own with hardly any help from his dad, and feeling she's had to be both
Worrying about money every month even though she works hard, and hating asking for help
Going back to college in her thirties was the thing she's proudest of because she'd always thought she was 'thick' at school
Worry about what she'll do when her mum can't manage on her own
Sometimes feeling lonely once Kieran's in his room of an evening, and not really fancying dating apps
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, camera slightly below eye level so it looks up a little. Daylight comes from a window to her left, with a ceiling light on as well, giving fairly even but slightly flat light. She has a round, friendly face, light freckling, a big open smile with crinkles at the eyes, and minimal make-up apart from a bit of mascara. Her hair is shoulder-length and dyed a warm blonde with darker roots showing, pulled back in a high ponytail with a few loose strands. No glasses. She wears a navy zip-up fleece with a small white leisure centre logo on the chest over a grey T-shirt, and a thin silver chain. Behind her: white kitchen cupboards with a few fridge magnets visible on the side of a fridge, a calendar with handwritten shifts on it, a kettle and a stack of plastic lunch boxes on the worktop, and a gym bag hanging on a door handle.
